instant.$description: 50ms — a near-instant state change. Used where content should appear without a perceived transition (the medium Accordion "snap" behaviour). Below ~100ms most users read the change as instantaneous.

fast.$description: 150ms — hover, focus and small colour or opacity changes. Short enough to feel immediately responsive to a pointer.

base.$description: 300ms — the default for disclosure, expansion and most component transitions. Matches the Chip and small-Accordion annotations.

slow.$description: 550ms — deliberate, attention-directing motion for large surfaces (the large Accordion open). Use sparingly; anything longer feels sluggish.

standard.$description: The default easing for elements moving within the viewport. Accelerates quickly, decelerates gently.

entrance.$description: For elements entering the screen — starts at full speed and decelerates. Pair with duration/base.

exit.$description: For elements leaving the screen — accelerates away. Pair with duration/fast; exits should be quicker than entrances.

ease-in-out.$description: Symmetric ease. Use for reversible state changes where neither direction should feel dominant. Used by the Progress bar fill transition and the large Accordion open.

bounce.$description: Overshoot easing for playful emphasis (the small Accordion open). Overshoots past the target then settles. Use rarely; it draws attention deliberately.

honour-preference.$description: System contract, not a per-component switch: every transition built from these tokens MUST collapse to an instant state change under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). Kept as a token so the requirement is discoverable in the token export rather than living only in documentation.
